name: ResearchRabbit
tagline: Literature discovery tool that maps related papers and authors.
best_for: Exploring a topic by following citations and related work
description:
ResearchRabbit is a literature discovery tool for finding academic papers connected to ones you already know. You add a few papers to a collection, and it suggests earlier work, later work and similar papers, often shown as a visual network.


It suits students starting a literature review, because a handful of seed papers can reveal clusters of related research and frequently cited authors. It is a discovery aid, so you still need to read the papers and judge their quality yourself. Plans and limits change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Create an account on the website.
Add a few known papers to a new collection.
Browse suggested related papers, authors and citation links.
Save useful papers and export them to your reference manager.

Helps find authors and related work
Good for early literature review stages
cons: Features and limits may change by plan
use_cases: Finding key authors in a field

name: Paperguide
tagline: AI research assistant for finding, reading and organizing papers.
best_for: Students and researchers who want AI help reading and summarizing papers
description:
Paperguide is an AI-assisted research workspace. It lets you search for academic papers, upload your own PDFs, ask questions about them and keep notes and references together in one place.


It is aimed at students and researchers who spend a lot of time reading papers. AI summaries and answers can speed up first-pass reading, but they can miss nuance or be wrong, so verify important claims against the original text before citing anything. Plans and limits change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Sign up on the website.
Search for papers or upload PDFs.
Ask questions or request summaries of a paper.
Save notes and references, then check key claims in the source.
use_cases: Skimming papers for a literature review
Extracting key points from a study
pricing_details: Pricing was not verified for this listing. Paperguide may offer free and paid options that change over time. Check the official website for current plans.

faq.a: Paperguide is a web-based AI research assistant for searching, reading, summarizing and organizing academic papers.

faq.q: Can I trust the AI summaries?
faq.a: Treat them as a starting point and confirm important details in the original paper.

name: Undermind
tagline: AI search agent for scientific literature.
best_for: Deep, targeted searches of scientific literature
description:
Undermind is a search tool built for scientific literature. You describe in detail what kind of paper or result you are looking for, and it runs a more thorough search than a simple keyword query, then returns a ranked list of relevant papers.


It is useful when a topic is specific or hard to describe with keywords, such as a particular method applied to a particular problem. As with any AI search, results can miss relevant work, so combine it with other databases and read the papers you rely on. Plans and limits change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Open the website and sign in.
Describe your research question in plain, detailed language.
Answer any clarifying questions and wait for the search to finish.
Review the results and follow up in other databases.
cons: Searches may take longer than keyword search
Coverage and limits depend on plan
use_cases: Finding papers on a niche method
Checking whether an idea has been studied
pricing_details: Pricing was not verified for this listing. Undermind may offer free and paid options that change over time. Check the official website for current plans.

faq.a: Undermind is an AI-driven search tool for finding scientific papers from a detailed description of what you need.

faq.q: Should it be my only search tool?
faq.a: No. Use it alongside databases such as Google Scholar to reduce the chance of missing relevant work.

faq.q: How do I get better results?
faq.a: Describe the problem, method and context in detail rather than a few keywords.

name: AskYourPDF
tagline: Chat-with-PDF tool for asking questions about documents.
best_for: Quickly querying long PDFs such as papers and reports
description:
AskYourPDF lets you upload a PDF and ask questions about it in a chat. Instead of scrolling through a long paper or report, you can ask for a summary, a definition or where a topic is discussed.


It is handy for study material, research papers and long reports. Answers are generated by AI and can be incomplete, so use the chat to find the relevant section and then read it yourself before quoting or citing. Plans and limits change, so check the official site for current plans.

Upload a PDF document.
Ask questions or request a summary in the chat.
Verify answers against the page text.

name: Inciteful
tagline: Free-to-explore citation network tool for finding related papers.
best_for: Mapping the citation network around a few papers
description:
Inciteful builds a citation network from papers you provide and then helps you explore it. It can surface influential papers, similar work and recent publications connected to your starting set.


It suits researchers and students who want to see how a field fits together and find key papers they may have missed. Like other citation tools, it is only as good as the citation data behind it, so treat it as a discovery aid alongside regular database searches. Plans and limits change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Open the website.
Enter one or more papers as a starting point.
Explore the network of related, similar and recent papers.
Save the papers you want to read.
pros: Helps find key and recent papers
cons: Interface may feel technical to beginners
use_cases: Spotting recent work on a topic
pricing_details: Pricing was not verified for this listing. Check the official website for current plans.

faq.a: Inciteful is a web tool that builds citation networks from papers you enter to help you discover related research.
Check the official website for current plans and any limits.

faq.q: Is it enough on its own?
faq.a: No. Combine it with database searches and your own reading.
